title: Join brothers and sisters tuples into siblings
description:
Join brothers and sisters tuples and assign it to siblings.

Python-Gym adaptation: implement as join_siblings(sisters, brothers), where sisters and brothers are tuples, returning their concatenation as a single siblings tuple (sisters first, then brothers).
hints: Joining two tuples together is called concatenation, and it produces one new, longer tuple.
Python lets you combine two tuples the same way you combine two strings or lists - with an operator, not a method.
Use the + operator: sisters + brothers puts every item of sisters first, followed by every item of brothers.
expected_behavior: Returns the concatenation of sisters and brothers as one tuple, sisters' items first.
solution:
def join_siblings(sisters, brothers):
    return sisters + brothers
explanation: The + operator on two tuples concatenates them into a new tuple, preserving the order: everything in the left operand comes before everything in the right operand.
